column1: l6/gar-nicht-gern|not like at all|I don't like cooking at all.|Scale: sehr gern (++), gern (+), nicht so gern (−), gar nicht gern (−−).

l6/himmelsrichtung|point of the compass|What are the four points of the compass called?|Himmel (sky) + Richtung (direction). Ending -ung → always die. The four directions from Lesson 2: der Norden, der Osten, der Süden, der Westen.
l6/schlecht|bad|At the weekend the weather is bad.|Opposite: gut. sch sounds like "sh"; ch after e is soft.
l6/wetterbericht|weather forecast, weather report|The weather report is short.|Wetter + Bericht (report). Compounds take the gender of the last word: der Bericht → der Wetterbericht.
l6/radio|radio|Dad is listening to the radio.|Stress the first syllable. im Radio = on the radio.
l6/internet|internet|I find the weather on the internet.|Stress the first syllable. im Internet = on the internet; im Internet surfen = to surf the web.
l6/sonnig|sunny|Tomorrow it will be sunny.|From die Sonne. A final -ig sounds like "-ikh".
l6/morgen-adv|tomorrow|Tomorrow it will rain.|Written in lower case: "tomorrow". Different from der Morgen (morning) in Lesson 5.
l6/steigen|to rise; to climb|At midday the temperatures rise.|ei sounds like "eye", st- like "sht". In forecasts: Die Temperaturen steigen = temperatures are rising.
l6/ueberall|everywhere|Today it's cold everywhere.|ü: round your lips as for "oo" but say "ee".
l6/temperatur|temperature|In the south the temperature is rising.|Stress the last syllable. Ending -ur → die: die Temperatur, die Natur.
l6/regen|rain|There's a lot of rain today.|Noun of regnen. No plural. Long e.
l6/schnee|snow|Tomorrow there will be a lot of snow.|Noun of schneien. ee is a long "ay". No plural.
l6/wind|wind|In the evening there's a lot of wind.|w sounds like v. Adjective: windig. Plural rarely used.
l6/bleiben|to stay; to remain|The weather stays good tomorrow too.|ei sounds like "eye". With weather: Das Wetter bleibt schön = the weather stays nice.
l6/minus|minus (below zero)|Today it's minus three degrees.|minus fünf Grad = −5 °C. You can also say: fünf Grad unter Null.
l6/plus|plus (above zero)|Tomorrow it will be plus eight degrees.|plus acht Grad = +8 °C. Usually just: acht Grad.
l6/heiss|hot|Today it's very hot.|ß = "ss", ei = "eye". Scale: sehr kalt – kalt – warm – heiß – sehr heiß.
l6/speisekarte|menu|Here's the menu.|Speise (dish) + Karte (card). sp- sounds like "shp"; s between vowels sounds like z.
l6/speise|dish, food|The dishes aren't expensive.|Kleine Speisen = small dishes, snacks. More formal than das Essen.
l6/imbiss|snack bar, food stand; snack|The snack bar isn't expensive.|Sells sausages, chips, burgers… Also means "a snack". ss because the i is short.
l6/ketchup|ketchup|The chips are good with ketchup.|Both der and das Ketchup are correct (der is used here).
l6/hamburger|hamburger|The hamburger costs five euros.|A final -er is soft like "a": "HAM-boor-ga".
l6/schinken|ham|I'm eating bread with ham.|sch sounds like "sh".
l6/dessert|dessert|For dessert there's ice cream.|From French: stress the last syllable, "de-SAIR"; the final t is silent.
l6/nehmen|to take; to have (when ordering)|I'll have a soup.|e → i and the m doubles: du nimmst, er/sie nimmt. Ordering: Ich nehme … Asking: Was nimmst du?
l6/kartoffelsalat|potato salad|Sausages with potato salad taste good.|Kartoffel + Salat; der Salat → der Kartoffelsalat. Stress the first part.
l6/apfelsaft|apple juice|The apple juice is cold.|Apfel + Saft; der Saft → der Apfelsaft. pf is said together.
l6/orangensaft|orange juice|The orange juice costs two euros forty.|Orange + n + Saft (an extra -n- makes it easier to say). der Saft → der Orangensaft.
l6/schokoladenkuchen|chocolate cake|The chocolate cake is very good.|Schokolade + n + Kuchen; der Kuchen → der Schokoladenkuchen. Long compounds: just cut them into parts.
l6/eis|ice cream; ice|For dessert I'm having an ice cream.|ei sounds like "eye". Eis = ice cream and also ice.
l6/einkaufsliste|shopping list|I'm writing a shopping list.|einkaufen + Liste with a linking -s-. Ending -e → usually die.
l6/dabeihaben|to have with you|Have you got the bread with you?|Separable as in Lesson 5: dabei + haben. dabei goes to the end: Hast du das Brot dabei?
l6/was-nimmst-du|What will you have? (du / Sie)||
l6/ich-nehme|I'll have … / I'll take …|I'll have the hamburger and a juice.|
l6/moechten|would like (polite)|I'd like a coffee.|Special forms: ich möchte, du möchtest, er/sie möchte, wir möchten, ihr möchtet, sie/Sie möchten. ich and er/sie are the same (no -t).
l6/lieber|rather, preferably|I'd rather drink tea.|Comparative of gern: gern → lieber (prefer). ie is a long ee.
l6/freund|friend (male); boyfriend|This is my friend Tim.|eu sounds like "oy": "froynt". Plural die Freunde: a group of friends, male or mixed.
l6/freundin|friend (female); girlfriend|This is my friend Lena.|-in for the female form; plural adds -nen: die Freundinnen.
l6/vielleicht|maybe, perhaps|Maybe it will rain tomorrow.|v sounds like f: "fee-LYKHT". Used when you're not sure.
l6/idee|idea|That's a good idea!|Stress the last syllable; ee is a long "ay". Gute Idee! = Good idea!
l6/problem|problem|I have a problem.|Stress the last syllable. Kein Problem! = No problem!
l6/hund|dog|I have a dog.|A final d sounds like t: "hoont". Don't mix up der Hund (dog) and der Hunger (hunger).
l6/mehr|more|We don't have any more juice.|kein … mehr / nicht mehr = no more / not any more. Long e.
l6/natuerlich|of course, naturally|Are you coming? – Of course!|From die Natur. Quick answers: Natürlich! / Klar!
l6/klar|of course; clear|Do you have time? – Yes, sure!|Ja, klar! = Yeah, sure! (informal).
l6/kein-problem|No problem!|Sorry! – No problem!|
l6/gute-idee|Good idea!|Shall we have a picnic? – Good idea!|
l6/na-gut|All right then. / Fine.|All right, then I'll have the salad.|Used when agreeing a little reluctantly.
l6/ach-nein|Oh no.|Oh no, it's raining!|
l6/ich-weiss-nicht|I don't know.|What will you have? – I don't know.|
l6/moment-mal|Wait a moment! / Hang on!|Hang on, where's my phone?|
l6/na-prima|Great!|The weather stays good. – Great!|
l6/lied|song|I like listening to a song.|ie is a long ee; a final d sounds like t: "leet".
l6/verein|club, association|My brother is in the football club.|Many Germans belong to a Verein: Fußballverein, Schachverein, Gesangverein…
l6/allein|alone|I'm not alone.|ei sounds like "eye". The song title Wir sind nicht allein = we are not alone.
l6/freizeit|free time, leisure|What do you do in your free time?|frei (free) + Zeit. ei = "eye", z = "ts": "FRY-tsite". No plural. in der Freizeit = in your free time.
l6/hobby|hobby|My hobby is photography.|Plural: die Hobbys (not Hobbies).
l6/schwimmen|to swim|We go swimming at the weekend.|schw- sounds like "shv": "SHVIM-men".
l6/tanzen|to dance|Lili loves dancing.|z sounds like ts: "TAN-tsen". The stem ends in z, so du tanzt (no extra s).
l6/grillen|to barbecue, to grill|On Saturday we're having a barbecue in the garden.|Related: der Grill.
l6/surfen|to surf; to surf the web|I'm surfing the internet.|Borrowed from English. im Internet surfen = to surf the web.
l6/ski|ski|Dad likes skiing.|Said "shee", not "ski". Ski fahren = to ski. Plural: die Skier.
l6/spass|fun|Dancing is fun!|sp- sounds like "shp", ß = "ss". Das macht Spaß! = That's fun!
l6/klub|club|The club is open on Saturday.|Also spelt der Club.
l6/krimi|crime novel, crime film|I like reading crime novels.|Short for Kriminalroman / Kriminalfilm.
l6/roman|novel|She likes reading novels.|Stress the last syllable: "ro-MAHN".
l6/toll|great, fantastic|I think dancing is great.|Informal, like super. Ich finde … toll = I think … is great.
l6/interessant|interesting|I find crime novels interesting.|Stress the last syllable.
l6/berg|mountain|The mountains are beautiful.|A final g sounds like k: "bairk". die Berge = the mountains.
l6/total|totally; really (informal)|I find that really interesting.|Spoken: total gern = love it; total toll.

l6/lieblings|favourite … (start of a compound)|My favourite colour is blue.|Lieblings + noun, gender from the last noun: der Lieblingsfilm, das Lieblingsbuch, die Lieblingsmusik, die Lieblingsfarbe, das Lieblingsessen.
l6/singen|to sing|We like singing together.|ng as in "sing".
l6/freunde-treffen|to meet friends|At the weekend I meet friends.|treffen (e → i): ich treffe, du triffst, er/sie trifft — seen in Lesson 5.
l6/mein-hobby-ist|My hobby is … / My hobbies are …|My hobbies are reading and swimming.|
l6/was-sind-deine-hobbys|What are your hobbies? (du / Sie)||
l6/das-macht-spass|That's fun!|Taking photos is fun!|
l6/ich-finde-toll|I think … is great / super / interesting.|I think hiking is great.|
l6/herbst|autumn, fall|In autumn it often rains.|Said together: "hairpst" (b → p).
l6/winter|winter|In winter it's cold.|w sounds like v: "VIN-ta".
l6/sommer|summer|In summer it's warm.|
l6/fruehling|spring|In spring the temperatures rise.|früh (early) + -ling. Also: das Frühjahr. Long ü.
l6/jahreszeit|season|Which season is it?|Jahr (year) + s + Zeit. z sounds like ts.
l6/reise|journey, trip|The trip to Vienna is great.|ei = "eye", s between vowels = z: "RY-zeh". Reiseland = a country to travel to.
l6/urlaub|holiday, vacation|In summer we go on holiday.|au = "ow"; a final b sounds like p. Urlaub machen = to go on holiday. Usually singular.
l6/wunderbar|wonderful|The weather is wonderful!|w sounds like v. Wunder (miracle) + -bar. Like: toll, super.
l6/natur|nature|I like hiking in nature.|Stress the last syllable (ending -ur → die). No plural.
l6/nord|North- / East- / South- / West- (start of a compound)|Hamburg is in northern Germany.|Written as one word: Norddeutschland (northern Germany), Süddeutschland, Ostdeutschland, Westdeutschland.
l6/windsurfen|to windsurf|My brother likes windsurfing.|Wind + surfen. w sounds like v.
l6/segeln|to sail|On holiday we go sailing.|Stem in -eln: ich segle (drop the e), du segelst, er segelt.
l6/programm|programme, schedule|What's the programme for tomorrow?|Stress the last syllable. Also a TV programme or software.
l6/mitte|middle, centre|In the middle of Germany there are many forests.|in der Mitte = in the middle. No plural.
l6/moeglichkeit|possibility; option|There are many options.|Ending -keit → always die. Freizeitmöglichkeiten = things to do in your free time.
l6/angebot|offer; what's on offer|In winter there's a lot on offer.|In tourism: Angebote für Wanderer = activities for hikers. When shopping: special offers.
l6/mountainbike|mountain bike|I like mountain biking.|Borrowed from English. Mountainbike fahren.
l6/klettern|to climb|We go climbing at the weekend.|Stem in -ern: ich klettere. Bergsteigen = mountaineering; klettern = rock climbing.
l6/insel|island|Malta is an island.|Short I, s sounds like z: "IN-zel".
l6/oft|often|In autumn it often rains.|Scale: immer > oft > manchmal.
l6/wald|forest, woods|We like hiking in the forest.|w sounds like v; a final d sounds like t. Plural: die Wälder.
l6/alpen|the Alps|The Alps are in the south.|Plural only: die Alpen. They run through southern Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
l6/dach|D-A-CH (Germany – Austria – Switzerland)|D-A-CH are three countries.|D = Deutschland, A = Österreich, CH = die Schweiz. Said like the word "Dach" (roof): "DAKH".
l6/aufgabe|task; exercise|My task is: calling customers.|au = "ow". At work: a task; at school: an exercise.
l6/buero|office|Ms Weber works in an office.|Stress the last syllable: "bü-ROH".
l6/kunde|customer (male)|The customer is calling.|Female: die Kundin. Plural: die Kunden.
l6/kundin|customer (female)|The customer buys a loaf of bread.|

l7/fernunterricht|distance learning|In distance learning we learn on the computer.|fern (far) + Unterricht (lessons). Episode 7: Walter learns hula hoop over the phone with Lara's remote help. Singular only.
l7/hula-hoop|hula hoop|Hula hoop is fun!|Borrowed from English. Also: der Hula-Hoop-Reifen = the hula hoop ring.
l7/reifen|hoop, ring; tyre|The hoop is too small.|ei = "eye". Here: der Hula-Hoop-Reifen. Also a tyre: der Autoreifen.
l7/schwingen|to swing|Mia swings the hoop very well.|schw- sounds like "shv". den Reifen schwingen = to swing the hoop.
l7/ueben|to practise|I practise the guitar every day.|Related: die Übung (exercise).
l7/weiter|further, on (continue)|We keep practising.|weiter üben = to keep practising. ei = "eye".
l7/wieder|again|I can ride a bike again.|ie is a long ee: "VEE-da". Don't confuse it with wie (how).
l7/schicken|to send|I'll send you a photo.|sch = "sh", ck = "k". ein Foto schicken = to send a photo.
l7/funktionieren|to work, to function|The phone doesn't work.|Stress "nee"; ti sounds like "tsi". For things and plans: Es funktioniert nicht = it doesn't work.
l7/kaputt|broken|The vase is broken.|kaputt sein = to be broken; etwas kaputt machen = to break something.
l7/vase|vase|The vase is beautiful.|In this loanword v sounds like v (VAH-zeh), unlike native German words (v = f).
l7/aussehen|to look (appearance)|Your photo looks good.|Separable as in Lesson 5 (and sehen: e → ie). Ask: Wie sieht das aus? aus goes to the end.
l7/stimmen|to be right, to be true|Is that right? – Yes, that's right!|st- at the start sounds like "sht": "SHTIM-men". Das stimmt! = That's right! Negative: Das stimmt nicht.
l7/tipp|tip, piece of advice|Do you have a tip for me?|gute Tipps geben = to give good advice.
l7/koennen|can, to be able to|I can swim well.|Modal verb: ich and er/sie have no ending (kann); the vowel changes ö → a. The main verb goes to the end in the infinitive.
l7/reiten|to ride (a horse)|Mia can ride very well.|ei = "eye". Add -e- before -st / -t: du reitest, er reitet.
l7/malen|to paint|He loves painting.|malen = to paint, colour in. (zeichnen = to draw, sketch.)
l7/backen|to bake|Lara is good at baking cakes.|Kuchen backen = to bake a cake. (Also du bäckst, er bäckt.)
l7/tennis|tennis|We play tennis on Sunday.|Singular only. Tennis spielen = to play tennis.
l7/klavier|piano|Ben plays the piano well.|Stress the last syllable: "kla-VEER". Klavier spielen = to play the piano.
l7/senkrecht|vertical, down (a column)|The numbers are in a column.|In Bingo: four in a column (senkrecht), in a row (waagerecht) or diagonally.
l7/waagerecht|horizontal, across (a row)|The words are in a row.|Opposite of senkrecht. aa = long "ah".
l7/kannst-du-gut|Are you good at …? (du / Sie)||Answers: Ja, (sehr) gut. / Ja, ein bisschen. / Nein, nicht (so) gut. / Nein, gar nicht.
l7/was-mache-ich-falsch|What am I doing wrong?|It doesn't work. What am I doing wrong?|
l7/kannst-du-mir-helfen|Can you help me?|Can you help me, please?|mir = "me" (comes later). Just learn the whole phrase.
l7/stricken|to knit|Grandma likes knitting.|st- at the start sounds like "sht".
l7/jonglieren|to juggle|Ben can juggle in the park.|j sounds like "zh" as in French (loanword). Stress "lee".
l7/einen-handstand-machen|to do a handstand|Can you do a handstand?|
l7/wollen|to want, to intend|I want to learn German well.|Modal verb: ich and er/sie have no ending (will). Stronger than möchten: your own will or plan.
l7/weiterbildung|further training, continuing education|Further training is important.|weiter (further) + Bildung (education). Singular only. Ending -ung → always die.
l7/kursangebot|range of courses|The range of courses is big.|Kurs + Angebot (Lesson 6). das Angebot → das Kursangebot.
l7/schule|school|The school is open on Monday.|sch = "sh", long u. In Germany, a Volkshochschule is an adult education centre.
l7/stress|stress|I'm very stressed.|st- at the start sounds like "sht": "SHTRESS". Singular only. Anti-Stress-Kurs = stress management course.
l7/kommunikation|communication|Communication is important.|Stress the last syllable; -tion sounds like "tsyohn". Singular only. Kommunikationstraining = communication training.
l7/training|training (session)|Training is in the evening.|Said the English way.
l7/psychologie|psychology|I find psychology interesting.|Stress the last syllable. y sounds like ü.
l7/theater|theatre; play|I like acting.|th = "t". Stress the middle: "te-AH-ta". Theater spielen = to act (in a play).
l7/produktion|production|Production starts on Monday.|Stress the last syllable. Musikproduktion = music production.
l7/mathematik|mathematics|I find maths hard.|Often shortened: die Mathe. th = "t".
l7/ferien|holidays (school, course)|In the holidays I want to sleep in.|Plural only. in den Ferien = in the holidays. Ferien = school holidays; Urlaub = time off work.
l7/wollen-wir|Shall we …? (suggestion)|Shall we go to the cinema?|Suggests doing something together. Yes: Ja, super! / Gute Idee! No: Nein, nicht so gern.
l7/was-willst-du|What do you want to …? (du / Sie)||
l7/ja-super|Yes, great!|Shall we go dancing? – Yes, great!|
l7/nein-nicht-so-gern|No, I'd rather not.|Shall we go jogging? – No, I'd rather not.|
l7/noe|Nope. (very informal)|Are you coming along? – Nope.|A casual "no", only with friends.
l7/politik|politics|I don't find politics very interesting.|Singular only.
l7/zeitmanagement|time management|In the course we learn time management.|Zeit + Management (said the English way).
l7/anfaenger|beginner|The course is for beginners.|Female: die Anfängerin. Spanisch für Anfänger = Spanish for beginners.
l7/gestern|yesterday|Yesterday I studied German.|st in the middle of a word is "st" (not "sht"): "GES-tern". gestern – heute – morgen.
l7/frueher|earlier, in the past, used to|I used to play a lot of football.|Long ü. Often with the Perfekt: Früher habe ich oft … gemacht.
l7/noch|still|Do you still remember the park?|Kennst du noch …? = Do you still remember …? (Different from noch einmal = once more.)
l7/p-machen|did, has done (machen)|What did you do yesterday?|machen → er macht → hat gemacht. Rule: ge + stem + t.
l7/p-kaufen|bought (kaufen)|I bought a loaf of bread.|
l7/p-lernen|learned (lernen)|We learned a lot.|
l7/p-spielen|played (spielen)|Lili played football with Tim.|sp after ge- sounds like "shp": "ge-SHPEELT".
l7/p-hoeren|heard, listened (hören)|I listened to music.|
l7/p-kochen|cooked (kochen)|Mia cooked soup.|
l7/p-arbeiten|worked (arbeiten)|He worked for a long time.|The stem ends in -t, so add -e-: ge-arbeit-et.
l7/p-wohnen|lived (wohnen)|We lived in Cologne.|
l7/p-ueben|practised (üben)|I practised the guitar.|
l7/p-lieben|loved (lieben)|I used to love ice cream.|
l7/p-sagen|said (sagen)|What did he say?|
l7/p-suchen|looked for (suchen)|We were looking for a flat.|
l7/p-kosten|cost (kosten)|The book cost ten euros.|The stem ends in -st, so add -e-: ge-kost-et.
l7/p-leben|lived (leben)|He lived in Vienna for two years.|
l7/p-fruehstuecken|had breakfast (frühstücken)|We had breakfast at the café.|
l7/p-grillen|barbecued (grillen)|On Saturday we had a barbecue.|
l7/p-tanzen|danced (tanzen)|We danced at the party.|
l7/p-fragen|asked (fragen)|I asked the teacher.|
l7/p-schicken|sent (schicken)|Walter sent a photo.|
l7/p-regnen|rained (regnen)|It rained yesterday.|
l7/p-essen|ate, eaten (essen)|I ate pizza.|essen → er isst → hat gegessen (ge…en).
l7/p-trinken|drank, drunk (trinken)|We drank tea.|
l7/p-sehen|saw, seen (sehen)|Have you seen the film?|
l7/p-lesen|read (lesen)|He read a book.|
l7/p-schreiben|wrote, written (schreiben)|I wrote an email.|
l7/p-sprechen|spoke, talked (sprechen)|We talked for a long time.|
l7/p-finden|found (finden)|Lara found the photo.|
l7/p-treffen|met (treffen)|I met friends.|
l7/p-schlafen|slept (schlafen)|You slept for a long time.|
l7/p-nehmen|took, taken (nehmen)|He took the hamburger.|
l7/p-singen|sang, sung (singen)|She sang a song.|
l7/p-bringen|brought (bringen)|Tim brought the tin.|Mixed form: it has -t but the stem changes: bringen → gebracht.
l7/p-haben|had (haben)|We had a lot of fun.|
l7/p-fernsehen|watched TV (fernsehen)|Dad watched TV for a long time yesterday.|Separable verb: ge- goes between the prefix and the stem: fern-ge-sehen.
l7/p-anrufen|called, phoned (anrufen)|I called Mum.|
l7/p-einkaufen|went shopping (einkaufen)|We went shopping at the supermarket.|
l7/p-aufraeumen|tidied up (aufräumen)|She tidied up the room.|
l7/p-telefonieren|talked on the phone (telefonieren)|I talked to Grandma on the phone for a long time.|Ending -ieren: no ge-.
l7/p-fotografieren|photographed (fotografieren)|He photographed the mountains.|Ending -ieren: no ge-.
l7/p-funktionieren|worked, functioned (funktionieren)|That didn't work.|Ending -ieren: no ge-.
l7/p-besuchen|visited (besuchen)|We visited Grandma.|The prefix be- doesn't separate and takes no ge-: besuchen → besucht.
l7/p-bezahlen|paid (bezahlen)|I paid for the coffee.|be- → no ge-.
l7/p-vergessen|forgot, forgotten (vergessen)|I forgot the bread.|ver- → no ge-; the participle looks exactly like the infinitive.
l7/p-gehen|went, gone (gehen)|We went to the cinema.|Moving from one place to another ⇒ use sein: gehen → er geht → ist gegangen.
l7/p-fahren|went, drove (fahren)|I went to Berlin.|
l7/p-kommen|came, come (kommen)|She came at eight o'clock.|
l7/p-wandern|hiked (wandern)|We hiked for three hours.|
l7/p-aufstehen|got up (aufstehen)|I got up at six o'clock.|
l7/p-bleiben|stayed; remained (bleiben)|The weather stayed good.|
l7/p-sein|was, been (sein)|I've been to Vienna before.|sein → ist gewesen. Bist du schon mal in Wien gewesen? = Have you ever been to Vienna?
l7/p-spazieren-gehen|went for a walk (spazieren gehen)|We went for a walk in the park.|
l7/einmal-mal|once|I've been to Vienna once.|schon einmal = once before, ever. Then: zweimal, dreimal …
l7/oefter|more often; quite often|I've cooked soup quite a few times.|Comparative of oft (Lesson 6). schon öfter = several times already.
l7/nie|never|I've never eaten sushi.|noch nie = never (so far). ie = long ee.
l7/unterricht|lessons, teaching|Lessons start at nine o'clock.|Singular only. Unterricht haben = to have lessons. Related: Fernunterricht.
l7/stunde|hour; lesson|I studied for two hours.|drei Stunden = three hours. st- at the start sounds like "sht": "SHTOON-deh".
l7/hast-du-schon-mal|Have you ever …?||haben or sein depending on the verb.
l7/ja-schon-einmal|Yes, once.||
l7/ja-schon-oefter|Yes, several times.||
l7/nein-noch-nie|No, never.||
l7/saxofon|saxophone|He plays the saxophone.|Also spelt Saxophon. Stress the last syllable.
l7/koenner|expert, skilled person|The course is for beginners and experts.|From können. Anfänger und Könner = beginners and advanced.
l7/schwer|difficult; heavy|The words are difficult.|schw- = "shv". Opposite: leicht.
l7/leicht|easy; light|Comics are easy.|ei = "eye". Opposite: schwer.
l7/cool|cool|I think that's cool!|Said as in English. Immer cool bleiben = always stay calm.
l7/zeitung|newspaper|I read the newspaper every day.|z = "ts", ei = "eye": "TSY-toong". From Zeit + -ung.
l7/meistens|mostly, usually|I usually study in the evening.|Scale: immer > meistens > oft > manchmal > nie.
l7/bus|bus|I learn vocabulary on the bus.|Short u. im Bus = on the bus.
l7/plakat|poster|We're making a poster.|Stress the last syllable. ein Plakat machen = to make a poster.
l7/comic|comic|I read comics in German.|Borrowed from English, said "KO-mik".
l7/vokabel|vocabulary word|I learn ten words every day.|In this loanword v sounds like v: "vo-KAH-bel". Vokabeln lernen = to learn vocabulary.
l7/leute|people|Many people learn German.|Plural only. eu = "oy": "LOY-teh". mit Leuten sprechen = to talk to people.
